title: focus.json
description: The current mood: a visual operating state, not just a notification switch. `work` is the default/resting state; `neutral` stays a hidden recovery mode, reachable only by an explicit manual write, never a fallback. The other moods each carry their own accent role, surface alpha, density, motion energy and notification policy (see Focus.qml's `moods` table — not duplicated here, same as theme.json naming a palette rather than embedding one). Also the firm-focus contract: read by the media browser and game launchers (refuse-to-start, with a reason) and by do-not-disturb; never by anything that would kill an already-running session.

mode.description: The active mood as WRITTEN, not necessarily as it reads once `until` has passed (see `previous`). `work` is the default, resting mode every mood without a manual choice reads as; every mode but `work` blocks the launches enforce.md lists (except launching into itself) until `until`, or forever if `until` is null. `neutral` stays a hidden recovery mode: it never appears in a picker and no fallback ever lands on it — only a deliberate manual write puts the pointer there.

until.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the mood lapses at, or null for an open-ended session that only an explicit `stop`/`set` ends. Past this timestamp the effective mode is `previous` (or `work`, the default, if `previous` is unset) — never `neutral`.

previous.description: The mode to fall back to once `until` passes, recorded at the moment a TIMED mode (one with `until` set) is entered: the effective mode of the pointer at that instant, or — if that pointer was itself a timed, unexpired mode — ITS `previous`, carried forward rather than nested. Cleared to null whenever an open-ended mode (no `until`) is entered. Absent/null on an expired timed mode falls back to `work`, never `neutral`.

source.description: Who last wrote this pointer. Absent/null means an existing store written before this field existed, or a write nothing bothered to attribute — treat that as `manual` for precedence purposes, since a pointer of unknown origin is safest treated as a deliberate choice rather than something a schedule may casually overwrite. Once a schedule can write this file alongside a keybind and a timer, the desk needs to say why it changed, not just what it changed to.

set_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the write that produced this state. Absent/null is the same backward-compatible case as a missing `source` — an older store, or one written before provenance existed. Exists so a precedence rule (and a human looking at the file) can tell a fresh manual choice from a stale one instead of guessing from `until` alone.
